title: Finite ell-power Tate lines and normalized quotient transition data
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $T$. Use the integral Tate line $L=\mathcal O_{E,T}(1)$ and signed tensor powers and duals of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For $n\geq0$ put $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^{n+1})_T$ with the actual constant quotient map $q_n:\mathcal O_{E,T}\to B_n$ and adjacent quotient $\tau_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Define $L_{n,1}=B_n\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}L$ using $q_n$, and $L_{n,m}=L_{n,1}^{[m]}$ for every integer $m$. A quotient-comparison family at level $n$ is a family of isomorphisms $c_m:B_n\otimes_{B_{n+1}}L_{n+1,m}\simeq L_{n,m}$. Its normalization predicate requires $c_1(s\otimes(t\otimes x))=s\tau_n(t)\otimes x$ on every local pure tensor and the signed unit, positive-power tensor recursion and inverse-positive-comparison dual formulas of [def-pur-signed-line-scalar-normalization-data]. Given a comparison family, define its semilinear transition $L_{n+1,m}\to\operatorname{Res}_{\tau_n}L_{n,m}$ as the canonical scalar-extension unit followed by $\operatorname{Res}_{\tau_n}(c_m)$. These are definitions of sheaves, data and a predicate; no normalized family's existence is asserted.
